brief: A stainless steel shaft collar. The outer diameter is 30 mm and it is 12 mm long. A 16 mm bore runs all the way through on the axis. One 5 mm set screw hole passes through the wall from the outside into the bore, halfway along the length. It carries no load - it is a locating collar, so there is no load case.

requirements.statement: The collar's outer diameter shall be 30 mm, measured across X.
requirements.rationale: Stated outer diameter; collar is round so X and Y both carry this figure.

requirements.statement: The collar's outer diameter shall be 30 mm, measured across Y.
requirements.rationale: Stated outer diameter; collar is round so X and Y both carry this figure.

requirements.statement: The collar's overall length shall be 12 mm.
requirements.rationale: Stated axial length of the collar.

requirements.statement: The through bore shall be 16 mm in diameter, on the collar's axis, running the full length.
requirements.rationale: Stated bore size; the shaft the collar locates onto.

requirements.statement: The set screw hole shall be 5 mm in diameter, passing radially through the wall into the bore, located halfway along the collar's length.
requirements.rationale: Stated set screw hole size and axial location.

requirements.statement: There shall be exactly one set screw hole through the wall into the bore.
requirements.rationale: Brief states a single set screw hole.

requirements.statement: The part shall be round about its axis.
requirements.rationale: The brief gives this part's size as a diameter, or calls it round.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 1 open hole of 16 mm down the part's axis.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 1 open hole of 5 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

assumptions.statement: The collar is made from a general-purpose austenitic stainless steel, e.g. 303 or 304 stainless.
assumptions.rationale: Brief states 'stainless steel' without a grade; 303/304 are the conventional choices for a non-load-bearing locating collar, chosen for machinability and corrosion resistance.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a different grade is required (e.g. 316 for marine/chemical exposure, or 17-4PH for higher strength), corrosion resistance or mechanical properties may not meet the actual service environment.

assumptions.statement: The 16 mm bore is concentric with the 30 mm outer diameter.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes the bore as running 'on the axis', implying concentricity with the OD.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: An eccentric bore would produce uneven wall thickness and could cause the collar to bind or wobble on the shaft.

assumptions.statement: The set screw hole is oriented radially, perpendicular to the bore axis.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes the hole as passing 'through the wall from the outside into the bore', which is the conventional radial orientation for a set screw.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A non-radial hole would not allow a standard set screw to bear on the shaft.

assumptions.statement: The set screw hole is threaded (tapped) to retain a set screw, rather than a plain clearance hole.
assumptions.rationale: A 'set screw hole' conventionally implies a tapped hole to retain the screw; no clearance/counterbore feature was mentioned.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the hole is meant to be a plain clearance hole with a separate nut or insert, the design would need a different feature and fit.

assumptions.statement: The collar operates in an ordinary indoor mechanical environment at ambient temperature, with no unusual chemical exposure beyond what stainless steel is typically chosen for.
assumptions.rationale: No environmental or temperature conditions were stated; this is the conventional default for a locating collar.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Extreme temperature or aggressive chemical exposure could require a different material grade or finish.

unknowns.question: Which grade of stainless steel is required (e.g. 303, 304, 316, 17-4PH)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Grade affects machinability, corrosion resistance and strength; this is recorded as a moderate-risk assumption (303/304) but should be confirmed before release.

unknowns.question: What thread specification (e.g. M5x0.8) and depth is required for the set screw hole, and is it a blind tapped hole or does it break through into the bore as a plain hole with threads only in the outer wall?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Determines the hole's thread callout and depth, which affects manufacturability and whether a standard set screw will seat correctly.
unknowns.suggested_default: M5x0.8 tapped through the wall into the bore

unknowns.question: What dimensional tolerances apply to the bore, OD and length (e.g. bore fit class against the shaft)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Determines whether the collar slides freely or is a tighter fit on the shaft; affects function but not catastrophic if deferred.
unknowns.suggested_default: Standard commercial tolerance, +/-0.05 mm on bore

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_ROUND: the brief calls this part round, and two equal bounding boxes do not say a part is round -- a 25 mm square block has a 25 by 25 box exactly as a 25 mm cylinder does. One run asked for a shaft collar and got a square block with both extent claims passing. This measures the built surface: 1 is a cylinder, a square is 0.707.

added REQ_HOLES_16MM_ON_AXIS: the brief states 1 open hole of 16 mm down the part's axis, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_5MM: the brief states 1 open hole of 5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

document.name: Shaft locating collar
document.description: A 30 mm OD x 12 mm long stainless steel collar with a 16 mm through bore and a single radial M5 set screw hole threaded into the wall at mid-length.
